title: "Kamp Kanawana History" -- presented at Training Course, June 6, 1951
note: Read end to end 2026-09-02 when the operator asked what it says. Five pages. Previously read_state 'extracted' with no cached text -- nine facts quoted it. Full text now cached. Yielded the Lake Wilson naming (resolving a CRITICAL open question), Lake Kanawana's former name (Lake St. Louis), 1900 attendance, the 1910 site-search narrative, and a correction to a mis-bracketed quotation.

title: A History of Kamp Kanawana (1935 Season Chronicle)
note: Well mined already -- nearly every event was extracted. Missed: six named individuals (best-camper shields, regatta winners, an outhouse prank, a staff swap) and a dollar figure recorded as $5 for $55. Three further names are lost to the OCR in the August shield sentence and cannot be recovered from this scan.

title: Concordia AtoM - Kamp Kanawana sub-series P0145/12B (full finding aid)
note: Also well mined at the collection level. What was missed was ITEM TITLES: a 1910 first-year report, a 1927 programme-philosophy paper, and winter ski camp records dated 1945-1947 that contradict winter-programming.md's 'summer-only until the 1970s'. Confirms Camp Becsies is real, settling an OCR guess in the 1951 history.

title: Kamp Kanawana Annual Report 1964
note: HEAVILY UNMINED. Ten new facts from one report. Four section directors named, none previously in the KB. Julien Tasse named three times as caretaker with his family and housing described, disproving the julien-tasse article's claim that no camp document names him. The 1964 international staff list matches the undated Pathfinder paddle's six origins, dating it. A 120-acre land purchase, one lot bought jointly with the Boy Scouts' Camp Tamaracouta.

title: Kamp Kanawana Annual Report 1965
note: Nine new facts. Co-ed camping proposed for 1966 with a full design, two years before the pilot this wiki dates to 1967-70, plus the Farquharson survey behind it. First T-Group staff training with four named trainers including Rix Rogers. The Kanawana-Tamaracouta Trail opened. The camp bell cracked. Mrs Tasse documented as staff. Rangers shown as a 1950s camper section in the ten-year table.

title: Kamp Kanawana Annual Report 1966
note: Two facts had been taken from this report -- the all-camp day list and the L&V result -- and everything else left. The report is almost entirely statistics: pre-season hours and costs, season consumption and programme hours, a payroll working out to 27.1 cents an hour, a ten-year summary with religion and age breakdowns, and a camper geography by Montreal district. Also states the camp's own claim of seventy-three years of CONTINUOUS operation from 1894.

title: Kamp Kanawana Annual Report 1969
note: Better mined than most (8 prior facts: the drowning, Anderson's appointment, the coed register). Still missed: the CIT programme going co-ed and dropping table-waiting in the same year, with 12 male and 4 female CITs building a model camp on Lake Wilson; 1969 outside groups and 125 weeks of camperships; horseback riding and stables two years before the finding aid's date; and Anderson's argument for year-round use of the property.

title: Kamp Kanawana Annual Report 1970
note: First Cystic Fibrosis campers. The fullest early-coeducation account in the project. Becsies and Page's identified as areas OF the Kanawana property, with transient young people camping at Becsies and a couple living at Wilson. Fourteen renting groups named. Kitchen catered out for the first time. Julien Tasse named for the third consecutive report.
